But beneath all of the stories he produced was a deep belief in the goodness of people—and a lifelong commitment to putting that belief into action."

He continued, "Together, he and his wife lived lives defined by purpose. They will be remembered for the values they championed and the countless people they inspired. We send our deepest condolences to all who loved them."

The actor, who was directed by Rob in 1986's Stand By Me, shared a photo of himself on set with the director on Instagram, simply saying, "Love you, Rob. Sincerely."

"I don't mean this as any offense to my parents—Rob was like a father to me," he added on CBS Mornings Dec. 15. "He was like a father to me. It's just surreal."

Jerry continued, "Everything I have is because of Rob Reiner. Everything I have. It's just a shocking day."

The family of the late television icon released an emotional statement noting how close the duo were.

"The Lear Family is devastated by the deaths of Rob and Michele Reiner," they told Deadline. "Norman often referred to Rob as a son, and their close relationship was extraordinary, to us and the world."

"Norman would have wanted to remind us that Rob and Michele spent every breath trying to make this country a better place," the statement continued, "and they pursued that through their art, their activism, their philanthropy, and their love for family and friends. Lyn Lear had remained very close with them and said, 'The world is unmistakably darker tonight, and we are left bereft.'"

"Christopher and I are numb and sad and shocked about the violent, tragic deaths of our dear friends Rob and Michelle Singer Reiner," Jamie Lee said in a statement to Variety, "and our ONLY focus and care right now is for their children and immediate families and we will offer all support possible to help them."

The couple added, "There will be plenty of time later to discuss the creative lives we shared and the great political and social impact they both had on the entertainment industry, early childhood development, the fight for gay marriage and their global care for a world in crisis. We have lost great friends. Please give us time to grieve."

After news of Rob and Michele's passing broke, the Magic of Belle Isle star wrote on Instagram of her director and his wife, "God be with those who love them. Thank you Rob for giving us so much joy to hold on to."

"The humor is smart and the heart is real," the actor, who costarred with Rob's dad Carl Reiner in 2003's Good Boy!, shared on X. "His films were part of the air for us. Grateful for what he made, and for what he and his wife gave the world.

The Monty Python alum tweeted that he had spoken to Rob on the phone the night before his death.

"Rob Reiner was a lovely man. I spoke to him last night for over an hour," he wrote on X. "I always enjoyed his company. I met him at his Dad's in 1975. He was telling me about fiming at Stonehenge and his thoughts for the future. This is so awful. I shall miss him. A clever, talented and very thoughtful man. So awful."

The Misery star said she was "absolutely devasted" by the news of Rob's death.

"I loved Rob," Kathy, who worked with the director in the 1990 film, told NBC in a statement. "He was brilliant and kind, a man who made films of every genre to challenge himself as an artist."

She continued, "He changed the course of my life. Michele was a gifted photographer. She shot my beautiful photos for the Misery campaign. My heart breaks for them both. My thoughts are with their family."

"Shocked by the death of Rob Reiner," the actor shared on X, 40 years after working with the director in 1985's The Sure Thing. "A great man."

The actor, who worked with the director in the 1994 movie North, wrote on X, "Horrified to hear of the passing of Rob Reiner and his wonderful wife Michelle [sic]. So much love to their kids and family."

"Rob Reiner was an almost indescribably wonderful man," she wrote on X. "Kind, jovial, thoughtful, and generous. He shaped our industry of course, and more so the world around us, making films that centered empathy and humor. He made us more bold, willing to take risks for love. He used his massive audience and knowledge of how to tell stories to defend democracy, and stand for his neighbors, both near and far."

"And even when the cameras were off, he showed up," Sophia went on. "He was often first to say yes to the organizing work, showing up on zoom after zoom, in support of organizations making the world a better place. He offered his talents and gifts. He said YES in service of others. In the years I’ve been lucky enough to know him in those dedicated spaces, he has influenced and inspired me, for good. I am utterly heartbroken at his and Michele’s deaths, and I am holding his loved ones in my heart today."

"Rob Reiner was one of my favorite directors," the Zoolander alum shared on X. "He made some of the most formative movies for my generation. He came out form behind a huge comedic shadow of the great Carl Reiner and being a tv actor to being a a great director who made an incredible run of movies."

He continued, "Spinal Tap is one of the best comedies ever made—and the list goes on. He was a kind caring person who was really really funny."

"This man's work changed my life and I don't think that's hyperbolic," the Bear actress wrote on her Instagram Stories. "I was so fortunate to have met him recently and couldn't believe how game he was to talk to me—and now just because he wanted to indulge a young fan."

She continued, "But because he really loved what he did and the friends he got to do it with. He was so generous with his time and energy and stories. Feeling absolutely gutted."

"I’m absolutely shocked and horrified to hear about Rob Reiner and his wife Michele," the comedian wrote on X. "This is a travesty. Praying for swift justice. Sympathies to their family and children. I’m at a loss for words."

"Grieving the loss of my favorite director of all-time," the Emmy winner shared on Instagram. "A Few Good Men is THE reason I became an actor, and Rob’s filmography behind the camera is THE reason I wanted to direct and still do."

He added, "I hate that Rob and his wife are gone from this world, but they sure as hell impacted me and countless others while here."

In the wake of Rob and Michele's death, the musician recalled meeting the couple while working on the yet-to-be released Spinal Tap at Stonehenge: The Final Finale.

"He and Michele made me feel like family and gave me an incredible opportunity to fulfill a dream," Josh shared on Instagram. "There was laughter and love and song and it was a memory I will cherish forever. I'm stunned and deeply saddened and sending my love to their family.

#757. There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson

Spaniard may feel some of Old Trafford’s allure when he goes there on Sunday but he is right in wanting to stay at the club with brighter prospects

On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title?

Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes.

Imagine being the manager who does sort it out. Imagine following in that brief lineage of United title winners: Ernest Mangnall, Matt Busby, Alex Ferguson … me? United remain the eighth wealthiest club by revenue in the world; imagine the resources that would be available if they were actually any good.

That is an allure that very few clubs in the world can match, no matter how good they were in the 1890s, and no matter how much the Villa owner, Nassef Sawiris, may dislike the fact. This is a point that cannot be made too strongly. Villa’s threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher was an outrageous attack on free speech. There is no way Carragher’s comment about the food chain of football could be construed as defamatory and, while it’s true he might have made the comment in less provocative terms, swearing is not a crime. This was a classic case of a legal threat being used to quell criticism and those fans – and, worse, journalists – who cheered it on should be thoroughly ashamed. The partisan blindness and persecution complex shared by fans of so many clubs is one of the most depressing features of the modern game.

But it’s also true United’s allure has come to look distinctly tarnished. No matter how bullet-proof a manager’s self-confidence, it would represent a remarkable risk to make the leap from Villa to United at this juncture. In almost every facet, from infrastructure to personnel, the modern Villa are better run than the modern United. And from Emery’s point of view, it’s not just that Villa are well run, it’s that they’re well run in his way.

He has the coaching staff he wants, while the president of football operations, Roberto Olabe, and the director of football operations, Damian Vidagany, are people he trusts and has worked with before. Emery would not have the degree of autonomy he has at Villa at many other clubs. United’s win over Roma on Tuesday may have eased the most immediate pressure on Michael Carrick, but nobody surely thinks that one good half against a depleted Serie A side cures all ills. (The question, obviously, is slightly absurd: nobody surely thinks Carrick is really the problem at United; it’s just that executives tend to get rid of managers because it’s what you do when there’s been a slump in form; it’s how a director acknowledges that he’s recognised there is a problem, while hoping desperately to deflect attention from his own shortcomings).

It doesn’t help that there is a clear precedent from five years ago, when a popular former United player saw his team come from two down to beat a Serie A side managed by Gian Piero Gasperini; Ole Gunnar Solskjær was sacked a month later.

The United crisis may have eased, but it is far from over. While Sir Jim Ratcliffe shows off architects’ plans and begs for public money to build a new stadium, Villa get on with building the new Trinity Road Stand. While United’s squad sags under the weight of its many contradictions, a weird mismatch of ill-fitting parts, Villa’s begins to take shape despite making 11 signings in the summer – even if the 3-0 defeat by Barcelona in midweek suggests there is still work to be done. They probably wouldn’t ideally have made such radical changes and would have preferred to keep Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa but, equally, there was an admirable sense of realism at Villa – a recognition of their place in the food chain, you might say – that when Chelsea or Arsenal come calling and offering huge contracts, there’s not much to be done other than to drive the price as high as possible.

Youri Tielemans is another player Villa might have liked to keep, but once United matched his release clause, the deal was done. Although Tielemans probably appreciates his new contract, it’s far from clear it’s been a good move for him from a football point of view, not least because United’s is a midfield that exposes his lack of mobility. Carlos Baleba was signed from Brighton to address that lack of dynamism in the United midfield but there were concerns about his tendency to drift in and out of games even before he suffered a hamstring injury on Tuesday.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

It even feels as though Villa have been smarter about using United players than United have. Victor Lindelöf was brought in on a free transfer in summer 2025 and has excelled since and while Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho had less of an impact, Villa only signed them on loan. Rashford’s time, which featured four goals in 17 appearances in all competitions, was probably the more eye-catching, but Sancho made 39 appearances in his season at Villa.

In both cases, Villa got value out of a players whose futures were uncertain but without committing to having to take them on full-time.

It’s pretty hard to imagine at the moment, but at some point, United will start heading in the right direction. It may even be that Tuesday’s win prompts a surge of adrenaline that takes them into the top half of the table. For now, though, Villa look by far the brighter prospect, a club on the up, while United are in barely managed decline.

#756. Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom

Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

This blog is now closed. Here are the main headlines from and about Germany on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The biggest news story out of Germany this evening had to do with the Left candidate Elif Eralp having sparked controversy with internal remarks to Der Spiegel.

A German news magazine's decision to publish private interview notes has sparked a controversy surrounding Berlin's potential next mayor.

On Thursday, Der Spiegel published internal comments on an interview by Elif Eralp, who led the socialist Left Party (Die Linke) to victory in September's state election. Her office had accidentally included the remarks while approving an interview for publication.

In the notes, Eralp expressed fears for her family's safety if she publicly named Ibrahim Ibrahim, a pro-Palestinian activist who is reported to have links to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), which the EU designates a terrorist organization. Ibrahim had attended the Left Party's election-night celebrations and was photographed with prominent Left Party Bundestag member Ferat Koçak.

Eralp also cited advice she received from Berlin police against publicly naming individuals linked to organized crime, though that advice was reportedly related to a separate case. Der Spiegel questioned whether her fears could affect her independence as mayor. Eralp rejected suggestions that she could be intimidated and pledged firm action against terrorism and organized crime.

The timing is significant. Eralp, the daughter of Turkish immigrants, could become Berlin's first Left Party mayor and the first woman of Turkish descent to hold the office. Her party won 25.7% of the vote in September's election and hopes to form a government with the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens. Both prospective partners have approved formal coalition negotiations.

The Left must decide whether to follow suit at a party conference this Saturday, October 31. The far-left party is also facing accusations of antisemitism involving some of its members. Newly elected lawmaker Vanessa Emde faces possible exclusion from the Left's parliamentary group following comments questioning whether states, including Israel, have an inherent right to exist. The Left has been part of Berlin coalition governments before but has never led one. The controversy comes at a pivotal moment in its effort to do so.

Germany's leaders are on a foreign relations push, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz on a trip to South Korea, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul in Panama and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in China.

Merz spoke of the threat North Korea posed to Europe's freedom by supplying troops to fight in Russia's invasion of Ukraine. He wraps up his visit with a trip to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Friday.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, meanwhile, is in Panama where he is visiting ahead of traveling to Atlanta for the G20 meeting.

Wadephul is there to promote free trade and also handed over humanitarian supplies to his Panamanian counterpart Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez.

And then German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier ditched the formalities in China and picked up a ping-pong paddle for a game with Germany’s most famous table tennis player, Tino Boll, who is accompanying Steinmeier as a special guest on his state visit.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul landed in Panama on Wednesday evening for a visit.

After his arrival at Panama City airport, Wadephul handed over humanitarian supplies to his Panamanian counterpart Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez.

The aid shipment is made up of about 20 tons of supplies. Panama was hit by a powerful earthquake earlier this month.

The supplies include water filters, blankets, tarpaulins, cots and kitchen sets worth over €150,000 ($167,000).

More than 5,000 people are still being housed in emergency shelters, weeks after the magnitude-7.7 quake on October 9, which resulted in injuries and damaged hundreds of buildings.

Wadephul also thanked the Central American country for maintaining the Panama Canal "so responsibly and ensuring it is fit for the future, as well as more generally focusing on preserving balance in the region."

Restrictions on other sea routes due to the conflict in the Middle East has meant that the Panama Canal is more important to global trade than ever.

Wadephul is due to hold talks on Thursday with Martinez-Acha Vasquez and President Jose Raul Mulino.

Wadephul will travel to the US state of Georgia for the G20 summit in Atlanta on Friday and Saturday.

Several names are being floated to replace Frank-Walter Steinmeier as Germany's ceremonial head of state — including some that could be the first woman to hold the post.

After delivering his speech at Peking University, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier ditched the formalities to play ping-pong with Germany’s most famous table tennis player, Tino Boll.

In the university sports hall, the two faced each other, accompanied by two Chinese participants — a referee and the university president. Right from the start, Steinmeier downplayed his chances, and subsequently lost 1–7.

Boll, who won silver at the Beijing Olympics in 2008, is the most successful German table tennis player of all time.

He won several Olympic medals, as well as titles in World Cups and World Championships during his storied career, which saw him ranked as the number 1 player in the world in 2003, 2011 and 2018.

To this day, Boll remains one of the best-known Germans in China, where ping-pong is unofficially considered the national sport.

Boll is accompanying Steinmeier as a special guest on his state visit.

Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Thursday called on China to reduce economic imbalances between the two countries, as well as between China and Europe.

Steinmeier, who was speaking at the renowned Peking University, also urged China to work with Germany and other European nations to strengthen the international, rules-based order and "to advocate for peace and free global trade."

The German president, who holds a largely ceremonial role, spoke of his respect for China's rapid development in its economy, technology and politics, calling China a "defining world power."

But Steinmeier added, "With greatness and power comes great responsibility."

"We are not concerned about China's rise. We are watching how China rises," he said.

"We do not want to decouple from China; on the contrary, we want to structure trade in such a way that it continues to benefit both sides." This, he said, requires fair and uniform rules.

Steinmeier was referring to the high barriers European companies face when trying to operate in the Chinese market. Since China heavily subsidizes its exports to Europe, the European market comes under pressure too quickly.

This poses "the danger of one-sided vulnerability," Steinmeier said. Europeans cannot want this for their economy, just as "China does not want it for its economy."

He also called on China to exert more influence on Russia to bring the war in Ukraine to an end.

According to Steinmeier, China's interests are also at stake in this war, just as they are in the Middle East. As a major trading power, China also needs free sea lanes, intact supply chains, and a secure energy supply.

"The longer these conflicts persist, the weaker the global economy as a whole becomes — and with it, one of its largest economies: China," the president said.

Steinmeier addressed future issues in which China should take a particular interest: climate change and artificial intelligence. He appealed to his hosts, saying that when it comes to AI, "we should jointly establish international guidelines so that the technology remains under human control," he said.

On the final day of his state visit, Steinmeier will meet with China's leadership and hold talks with, among others, President Xi Jinping.

Steinmeier is making his first visit to China in eight years, as he seeks to boost bilateral ties.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday said North Korea was threatening "freedom throughout Europe" by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in its war against Ukraine.

After a meeting in Seoul with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Merz highlighted that Russia was supplying weapons to North Korea.

The chancellor said this arrangement therefore shows how "Korea's security affects Europe's security. And Europe's security also affects Korea's security."

North Korea has boosted its military ties with Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Pyongyang has provided Moscow with artillery ammunition and missiles. It has also, according to South Korean intelligence services, sent about 15,000 soldiers to fight alongside Russian forces.

In exchange, Russia provides financial backing, military technology and security guarantees to North Korea.

Before Merz's arrival on Thursday, North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the Sea of Japan, according to the South Korean military.

At the start of his visit, Merz said he hoped that Korea would eventually be unified. The peninsula has been split along the 38th parallel since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953.

Merz also agreed with Lee to deepen their two nations' strategic and security ties, which includes joint military exercises and exchange of intelligence.

The chancellor is expected to conclude his trip to South Korea with a visit to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Friday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Germany is looking for new partners in Asia. As Chancellor Friedrich Merz travels to Singapore, Japan and South Korea, Berlin is trying to reduce its economic dependence on China while adapting to a changing global order. But can countries in the Indo-Pacific, besides China, help Germany diversify its trade and security partnerships?

This week on Berlin Briefing, DW's Giulia Saudelli speaks with DW Business Reporter Steven Beardsley and DW Chief Political Correspondent Nina Haase, who is traveling with the chancellor.

They discuss Germany's push to "de-risk" from China, growing security cooperation in the Indo-Pacific, and whether middle powers can work together to shape the future global order.

Germany and South Korea on Thursday pledged to work together on the economy, energy and security and high-tech industries, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said.

The South Korean leader made the announcement after a meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Seoul.

At a joint press conference, Lee told reporters that he had asked Merz for Germany's backing in securing favorable treatment for South Korea as part of the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act.

The two leaders also agreed ​to ⁠improve bilateral ties to ⁠an "enhanced ​strategic partnership," Lee said.

An eight-year-old girl sustained serious injuries after she was attacked by at least one wolf at a wildlife park in Brandenburg in east Germany.

The child was brought to hospital by a rescue helicopter on Wednesday.

Local officials said a zookeeper had helped prevent other children from being attacked.

Police are investigating how and why the attack occurred, which took place during a special program for children.

Police on Thursday said their investigation was centered on a staff member who was in the enclosure with the children, a spokeswoman said.

The Teltow-Fläming district administration said the incident happened before the wildlife park's regular opening hours as part of an "Animal Keeper Day" for children.

The administration also said the attack had taken place in the polar wolf enclosure.

"While the animals in the wildlife enclosure were being watered, the wolves kept there attacked a girl and seriously injured her," the district administration said.

The zookeeper's quick action prevented "further harm to two other girls" who were also at the scene, the district added.

The park will remain closed for the time being, officials said, as authorities launch a safety review at the wildlife park, which is about 60 kilometers (37 miles) south of Berlin.

Police are still probing the circumstances that led to the children being inside the enclosure.

The Johannismühle Wildlife Park said it was cooperating with authorities but could not provide further details due to the open investigation.

"We deeply regret the incident, and the affected family has our full support," the park said.

The wildlife park was closed until further notice "due to technical reasons," a sign at the entrance said on Thursday.

A wolf bit a woman in a busy shopping area in Hamburg this year, in what is thought to be the first such attack since wolves were reintroduced to the country in 1998.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said at the start of his visit that he hopes North and South Korea will eventually be reunited.

The Korean Peninsula has been divided into two states since the Korean War ended in 1953.

Merz pointed to his own country's division between West and East Germany for much of the second half of the 20th century.

"Korea and Germany are united by the painful experience of division," he wrote in the guest book during his meeting with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung.

"I also wish for the people of Korea what we are fortunate to experience in Germany: unity in freedom."

North Korea is a largely isolated dictatorship ruled by Kim Jong Un, while the South is a democracy that has close ties with the West.

The two Koreas technically remain at war since a truce ended hostilities.

Merz is set to visit the demilitarized zone (DMZ), which divides the two countries, on Friday.

The German chancellor's visit to South Korea is the last stop on his tour of Asia this week, which has also seen him visit Japan and Singapore.

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has just returned home from the hospital, admitting that he hadn't listened to his body, "and then at some point, my body just said, 'Enough is enough!'"

Read our full report on Kompany's health and the need for better support for coaches at the highest level of sport here.

They were once top sellers in China. Now the likes of Volkswagen, Toyota and Honda are losing ground to a new generation of Chinese carmakers. What happened?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Volkswagen (VW) reported third quarter losses of €5.8 billion ($6.5 billion) on Thursday, as it faces rising competition from China.

Germany's biggest car maker had reported a loss of just over €1.07 billion in the same period last year.

Volkswagen, like other car makers, has struggled to keep pace with fierce competition from China, the world's biggest car market. VW has also struggled with the transition to electric vehicles and with declining demand.

Volkswagen last month warned that its 10-brand group, which includes makers such as Audi, Seat and Skoda, was facing a 10-billion-euro hit to its annual profits.

The most significant hit came from Porsche, Volkswagen's luxury sports car and SUV subsidiary. Porsche, which was once a major driver of profits for the VW group, was also one of the main factors behind VW's quarterly losses in 2025.

The luxury brand has been hit by a sales slump in China, US tariff policy and its electric vehicle strategy.

VW announced this year that it plans to cut over 100,000 jobs across the group by the end of the decade as it tries to reduce costs. It announced on Thursday that its restructuring would cost the company 31 billion euros.

The company is considering or has decided to shut down multiple German factories — including plants in Zwickau, Emden, Hanover, and Neckarsulm.

"What matters now is swift and consistent implementation," Arno Antlitz, VW's chief financial officer said in a statement. "We cannot lose any time and need to act quickly and decisively."

For more on this story, read our full report by DW's Mark Hallam.

#753. The Los Angeles Gift Guide for Cool Coastal Girlies

Whether she’s heading to Pilates, driving up the coast or lounging beachside, these California-cool gifts bring a little piece of LA sunshine to wherever she is this holiday season.

Welcome to gifting season with E!, where we’re making it easier to gift shop for the pickiest people on your list.

Finding the right present for the Los Angeles girly in your life can feel like a challenge. She likely has her favorite beauty products, her go-to workout class and probably a very specific matcha order. And in a city where a beach day can turn into sweater-weather by sunset, a gift she’ll actually use is your best bet.

We’ve been keeping tabs on the pieces and brands that Hollywood shopped all year long. So, let’s just say this lineup of buzzy LA-inspired gifts will be coveted by any Angeleno or pop culture-enthusiast. From roomy tote bags perfect for farmers-market runs to cozy layers for chilly beachside evenings, there’s something special at every price point—with picks starting under $30—for that LA angel on your holiday gift list.

You don't have to live in or be from the City of Angels to find gifts that any LA lover will enjoy. Consider LA-based brands for something a local would appreciate, like Lisa Says Gah!, MadHappy or Aviator Nation.

If she frequents Dodger Stadium, a standout baseball cap—whether with bows or polka dots— will get plenty of use. Is your Angeleno a foodie or hostess? Treat her to something she might not splurge on herself, like a fancy Cali-made olive oil and locally produced honey.

When in doubt, opt for a Gold Coast classic: a luxe robe or travel bag from the official Beverly Hills Hotel collection brings LA luxury to her home. And if she’s picky about her sartorial style, a thoughtful gift for her home, like a decorative ornament or pillow, is a lovely seasonal upgrade.

Keep scrolling for the best Los Angeles-themed gifts for the LA-loving girly in your life.

#752. Gisele Bündchen Honors "Great Man" Joaquim Valente in Birthday Tribute

Gisele Bündchen gave her husband Joaquim Valente a sweet shoutout for his 39th birthday: “How lucky I am. I love you so much!”

Gisele Bündchen’s husband Joaquim Valente has strutted his way into her heart—and he’s there to stay.

The supermodel gave the jiu-jitsu instructor some love in honor of his 39th birthday, sharing just how grateful she is to have him in her life.

“Today a great man was born, @joaquimvalente,” Bündchen wrote over a photo of the pair on Instagram Stories Nov. 7 in a message translated from Portuguese. “How lucky I am. I love you so much!”

In the sweet snap, Bündchen—wearing a mustard yellow halter top—cozied up to her husband as they both gave the camera a smile.

But this wouldn’t be the first time Bündchen and Valente—who tied the knot in December 2025—have proved they’re a model match.

After all, the Victoria’s Secret Angel—mom to a 19-month-old son with Valente as well as kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13, with ex-husband Tom Brady—received support from her partner as he stepped out with her for a rare public appearance at the Lotus House’s annual gala, where Bündchen was honored, in Miami, Fla., Oct. 29.

“I feel so grateful to be part of the Lotus House family and to witness all the love and care that [goes] into changing so many lives,” Bündchen wrote on Instagram following the outing. “I’m so honored to be part of this journey alongside the incredible @lotushouseshelter team, all the volunteers, and everyone who gives their time, love, and support in whatever way they can.”

In addition to sharing pics alongside fellow award honoree Karlie Kloss, the 45-year-old—dressed in a button-down shirt, denim jeans and a sun hat—also posted a group photo with Valente.

And it’s clear that the athlete—donning blue jeans, a gray button-down shirt and a brown vest—couldn’t have been happier to be his wife’s cheerleader as he leaned in close to Bündchen while giving the camera a bright smile.

But he doesn’t just show up for Bündchen when it counts. As the Lessons author emphasized on Father’s Day this past June, he also shows up as the best dad.

“Thank you for leading by example, and for the values you embody, love, humility, integrity, discipline, kindness and consistency,” Bündchen wrote in a June 21 Instagram carousel. “You are an incredible role model. We are all so grateful for you, and we love you so much.”

#750. Céline Dion Plays Air Bass at Metallica’s Sphere Show

The singer showed off her air-bass skills during Metallica's Life Burns Faster residency at Las Vegas' Sphere.

Céline Dion might be best known for her soaring power ballads, but the Canadian superstar proved she knows her way around a heavy metal concert, too.

The “My Heart Will Go On” singer was spotted enthusiastically playing air bass during Metallica‘s Life Burns Faster residency at Sphere in Las Vegas on Thursday (Nov. 5), with fan-filmed footage capturing her enjoying the performance from a suite inside the venue. Related Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75 Benson Boone Brings Young Fan Battling Cancer Onstage at Brisbane Concert Explore Celine Dion Guns N' Roses Metallica See latest videos, charts and news

In a video shared on Instagram by user @theordacityyy, Dion can be seen standing and mimicking the bass-playing techniques of Metallica‘s Robert Trujillo, enthusiastically moving her hands as the musician performed alongside guitarist Kirk Hammett.

The moment occurred during the band’s customary “Kirk and Rob Doodle,” an instrumental segment that gives Hammett and Trujillo an opportunity to jam together during the show. According to the concert’s reported setlist, the Nov. 5 installment incorporated “Motown Yo Town” and “Copenhagen.”

Dion wasn’t the only famous face taking in the performance. Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash was also reportedly spotted in the suite, while members of No Doubt were among the other musicians seen enjoying the concert.

Although Dion’s enthusiasm might seem unexpected to fans more familiar with her romantic ballads, her appreciation for Metallica is hardly newEarlier this year, the five-time Grammy winner shared a selection of songs from her personal playlist, which included Metallica’s 1996 single “Until It Sleeps.”

“Eddy, one of my twins, his favorite band is Metallica,” Dion said in the video, before enthusiastically attempting her own impression of frontman James Hetfield.

The appearance comes amid an eventful year for Dion, who returned to full-length concerts in September after a six-year absence. Her Paris residency marked a significant milestone following her 2022 announcement that she had been diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological disorder that had affected her ability to perform.

Dion, whose Billboard Hot 100 history includes four No. 1 singles — “The Power of Love,” “Because You Loved Me,” “My Heart Will Go On” and her R. Kelly duet “I’m Your Angel” — completed the first leg of her Paris comeback performances in October.

Meanwhile, Metallica’s Life Burns Faster residency launched at Sphere on Oct. 1, bringing the metal veterans’ No Repeat Weekend concept to the Las Vegas venue. The format, introduced during the band’s M72 World Tour, features different setlists across paired Thursday and Saturday concerts.

The band concludes the 2026 portion of its Sphere residency on Saturday (Nov. 7), with performances scheduled to resume in January 2027.

#749. Little Rascals Star Bug Hall Shares Financial Plea Ahead of Baby No. 6

Former child star Bug Hall—best known for his work in The Little Rascals—created a fundraiser asking for financial aid as he and wife Jill prepare to welcome baby no. 6: "There was no other choice."

Bug Hall is asking for help during a desperate time.

Nine months after The Little Rascals actor announced that he'd taken a “vow of poverty” while living off-the-grid with his family, he launched a GoFundMe asking for financial assistance ahead of the birth of his and wife Jill’s sixth baby.

“It's now six years since I self-cancelled, and I have avoided doing one of these in all that time,” Hall shared on the fundraiser’s page Nov. 5. “I always said this was my choice, and so I didn't want to offload the glorious burden of it unless there was no other choice. Well here we are.”

The former child star added that his soon-to-be family of eight—who live in a camper van in Mountain View, Ark.—“made it onto the new land in record time,” but are a “few materials short of having things working right.”

As Hall (real name Brandon Hall) admitted, “I've fallen a little behind on the few bills we have (phone, propane for the camper, and an unexpected electric hookup service fee).”

While the 41-year-old—best known for playing Alfalfa in the 1994 film The Little Rascals—emphasized that his family is “all overjoyed to be where they are” and they’re “even enjoying roughing it,” time is currently not on their side.

“Baby [No. 6] is less than a month away,” he wrote, “and I really need some help getting the last few things buttoned up beforehand.”

“My hope is to finalize everything here over the next two weeks,” the Get a Clue star added, “so I can take some work until the baby arrives.

But Hall—who previously shared in an April 2025 YouTube video that he and his wife were raising their five kids in a “radical Catholic extremist life”—noted that he welcomes and any all forms of support, not only financially.

“Times are hard for everyone, and I'm no more deserving than anyone else,” he wrote, “but I ask in your charity that you help where you can, whether monetarily, by sharing this, or by prayer and sacrifice for the Hall-Barnetts of the Holy Cross.”

Hall’s plea for assistance comes nearly one year after he detailed to the Daily Mail why he'd taken a “vow of poverty," revealing that he'd given up the money he earned from his acting career, which he quit in 2020 following his arrest for huffing air duster cans. (He told the Daily Mail he faced no charges.)

“My goal is to maintain a life as free of any need for an income as possible,” he told the outlet in an interview published Jan. 28. “If there's a financial need that comes up, I'll go take some work or do an odd job, for cash to fulfill that need.”

As Hall and his family continue to build their life off-the-grid, keep reading for more stars who have chosen to leave Hollywood…

After the Mask of Zorro actor suffered a near-fatal heart attack in 2019, he moved back to his native Málago, Spain, to focus on his love of theater.

“It changed the way I look at life,” Banderas told The Times in March 2026. “Faced with death, it made me look back and realise that I am, in fact, a theater actor.”

Now, the Tony nominee—who still occasionally takes on TV and film projects—owns a theater venue and gets involved with the local community.

“I have never been so happy,” he continued. “It keeps me in touch with my roots, my neighbourhood, my people. I haven’t lost that connection over the years. Quite the opposite.”

Before landing a role in Prime Video's Every Year After, The Girl Next Door actress took a four-year break from acting, leaving L.A. to raise her two kids with husband Dion Phaneuf.

"I realized I worked all four years through our first child and it was really hard," Cuthbert confessed in June 2026 during an appearance on Today, "to separate that mom from the working person I was. So, when we had our second, I just felt like I didn't want to waste any second of it and I didn't want to be on set."

Cuthbert—best known for starring in '00s films like Old School as well as hit TV shows including 24 and Happy Endings—added, "I just felt like I needed to be at home with the kids and I enjoyed every minute."

The actress, known for her roles on hit TV dramas like Fire Country, Numb3rs and Rescue Me, shared in July 2026 that she sold her Los Angeles home after living there for 30 years to embark on her "third chapter" somewhere far away from Hollywood.

"I came here chasing a dream that I am still shocked worked out," she wrote on Instagram. "And I also got to raise babies in the sun and the mountains and enjoy this beautiful home and attend public schools ?? Pinch me I’m overwhelmed by the blessings and hope, really hope I gave enough back. LA will always be where my family is from."

The Ellen DeGeneres Show host's eponymous talk show ended in 2022 after a 19-season run amid allegations of a toxic work environment that prompted an internal investigation, multiple firings of executives and public ire.

DeGeneres returned to the spotlight for her final standup special For Your Approval, which released on Netflix in September 2024. During the lead-up to that special, she revealed she would be leaving Hollywood altogether.

"This is the last time you’re going to see me," she told a crowd during her Ellen’s Last Stand…Up tour, per SFGate. “After my Netflix special, I’m done."

DeGeneres and her wife Portia de Rossi have since moved to the Cotswolds, deciding to stay put in November 2024 after Donald Trump's reelection, the talk show host told to Richard Bacon in a July 2025 conversation at the Everyman theater in Cheltenham.

"It's absolutely beautiful," she gushed about the English countryside, per the BBC. "We're just not used to seeing this kind of beauty. The villages and the towns and the architecture—everything you see is charming and it's just a simpler way of life.

"It's clean," DeGeneres continued. "Everything here is just better—the way animals are treated, people are polite. I just love it here. #747. Benson Boone Brings Young Fan Battling Cancer Onstage at Brisbane Concert

"I've had the opportunity of meeting a 13-year-old girl who is battling her second round of cancer," Boone told the crowd.

Benson Boone opened the Australian leg of his Wanted Man tour with a special guest. He brought a 13-year-old fan who is battling cancer onstage to sing “Beautiful Things” with him on her birthday. Explore Benson Boone See latest videos, charts and news

The moment came at the end of Boone’s set at Brisbane Entertainment Centre on Friday (Nov. 6). The Music reported that the singer stopped to introduce the final song. Related Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75 Céline Dion Plays Air Bass at Metallica's Sphere Show

“I’ve had the opportunity of meeting a 13-year-old girl who is battling her second round of cancer,” Boone told the crowd, according to the outlet. “It’s her birthday today and her birthday wish was to come on stage and sing ‘Beautiful Things.’”

The fan, Kenzie Riddle, then rose from an upper platform and joined Boone on the song. According to The Music, roughly 10,000 people were in the arena.

Riddle has Ewing’s sarcoma. As reported by Nine’s Today, she believed she had beaten the illness after about two and a half years of treatment, but the cancer returned and she is now facing intensive chemotherapy. Her family said they bought tickets to the show in July as her 13th birthday present. Her campaign to meet Boone took off online after a local musician, Fergus Hogan, shared an Instagram video about her story.

“I love his energetic style and how he’s so over the top,” Riddle told Today before the concert. “He’s kinda crazy and I love it.”

Her family also told the program: “She’s such an unbelievable inspiration to so many people… But I think even bigger than that is the community behind her.”

“Beautiful Things” was Boone’s breakout single. Released in January 2024, it reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the most-streamed songs in the world that year. Boone followed it with his debut album Fireworks & Rollerblades that April. His second album, American Heart, arrived in 2025 and included the single “Mystical Magical.”

The Brisbane show opened Boone’s Wanted Man tour of Australia. Boone has two additional Brisbane performances scheduled for Nov. 7 and 8 before the tour heads to Melbourne for three concerts at Rod Laver Arena beginning Nov. 12. The Australian leg concludes with three shows at Sydney’s Afterpay Arena from Nov. 17-19.

#746. The palaeo cave art that hid in plain sight for 26,000 years

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Chris Simms is a science writer based in Somerset, UK.

Inscriptions at the Cova de la Font Major cave system in Catalonia in northeastern Spain prompts rethink of prehistoric population and cultural trends. Credit: Vergès Bosch, J. M., Salas-Altès, M./Antiquity

Inscriptions at the Cova de la Font Major cave system in Catalonia in northeastern Spain prompts rethink of prehistoric population and cultural trends. Credit: Vergès Bosch, J. M., Salas-Altès, M./Antiquity

Archaeologists have described hundreds of rock-art engravings dating back around 26,000 years in a cave frequently visited by tourists in Catalonia — a region of northeastern Spain that was thought to be almost devoid of palaeolithic art1. The findings were published in the journal Antiquity on 5 November.

Josep Maria Vergès Bosch, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES-CERCA) in Tarragona, Spain, spotted some prehistoric engravings among more-modern graffiti in the Cova de la Font Major during a planned excavation in 2019.

Vergès and archaeologist Míriam Salas-Altès at IPHES-CERCA studied 280 Palaeolithic art motifs, including 55 animal depictions, from the cave. “The sheer quantity of art discovered at the Cova de la Font Major is exceptional,” says Salas-Altès.

The cave system — made up of more than 3.5 kilometres of underground passageways that have been occupied numerous times during human history — has been open to the public for some seven decades and became a museum in the 1990s.

The drawings were easy to miss. “When you shine a light straight on the engravings, they are really difficult to see, you have to play with light from different directions to see the depressions,” says Salas-Altès.

Researcher Míriam Salas-Altès documents engravings in a tunnel of the cave system. Credit: Josep Maria Vergès/IPHES-CERCA

The etchings include images of animals such as a horse, a bear and an aurochs (the ancestor of domestic cattle), as well as myriad swirling lines. A handful of the engravings reveal how the artists used “natural lines or fissures in the walls”, says Salas-Altès. For example, “one is used to represent the ground under a horse”.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03585-z

Vergès Bosch, J. M. & Salas-Altès, M. Antiquity https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2026.10447 (2027).

#744. Elvis Presley Rights Owners Sue Suno Over AI Voice Cloning: ‘Elvis’ Identity Was Stolen’

The singer's legendary voice is at the center of a cutting-edge lawsuit that aims to hold the AI firm legally liable for allowing users to create knockoff vocals.

The owners of Elvis Presley’s intellectual property are suing Suno in a new lawsuit that claims the artificial intelligence music company violated the King of Rock ‘n’ Roll’s likeness rights by stealing his voice.

Weeks after suing AI giant Anthropic for training Claude on Elvis songs, the new case filed Friday (Nov. 6) by Elvis Presley Enterprises levels similar copyright accusations against Suno, the leading AI music firm. But it also includes legally-novel allegations that Suno broke the law by letting users clone Presley’s “unmistakable and iconic voice.”

“All of the humanity, history, despair, and triumph that constitutes Elvis’ identity was stolen and is stored on servers and harnessed by Suno to make massive amounts of money,” writes Richard Busch, a veteran music litigator at the firm Adams & Reese who filed the case. “Suno did so intentionally, maliciously, and fraudulently to financially benefit itself and artificially compete with Elvis’ likeness and copyrights, and continues to do so to this day.”

The new lawsuit marks one of the first major cases under a new Tennessee law, coincidentally called the ELVIS Act, that was recently enacted to address problems caused by AI. The first-in-the-nation statute was touted as a weapon against people who create illegal deepfakes, but it also allows for lawsuits against tech firms that enable such voice and image cloning in the first place.

Taken together with the Anthropic case, the suits over Elvis represent easily most significant action filed on behalf of an individual musician over AI — in this case, arguably the most famous recording artist of all time. Suno and Anthropic were already facing cases from music labels accusing them of infringing millions of copyrighted songs to train their models, as well as a class action by smaller artists who similarly say Suno stole their likenesses.

Friday’s lawsuit was filed by Elvis Presley Enterprises, a unit of the licensing giant Authentic Brands Group that controls the intellectual property tied to Elvis, including much of his song catalog and the rights to his name, image and likeness. In a statement to Billboard on Saturday, ABG spokeswoman Lark-Marie Antón said the new lawsuit and its evidence “speak for themselves.”

“The name, image, likeness, and music of Elvis Presley are among the most valuable intellectual property assets in the world,” Antón said. “We protect those rights vigorously.”

In statement Saturday responding to the lawsuit, a Suno spokeswoman told Billboard: “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. We are always working to strengthen our guardrails and we will continue to add new safeguards that protect artists and our users.”

The looming battle with Suno will raise untested legal questions about the extent to which AI companies can be sued for allegedly ripping off a musical artist’s identity. The use of AI to convincingly mimic real people has been one of the booming technology’s most controversial applications, and no where less so than an industry largely built on famous singing voices.

“Elvis’ voice possessed a distinctively rich vocal timbre, with a warm velvety resonance and perfectly employed vibrato, coupled with his ability to vary his technique and delivery within the same song as well as across several different styles of music, which became his immediately recognizable musical signature across the world,” the lawsuit says.

Suno has argued in other lawsuits that its current models do not allow users to include the names of specific artists in prompts, nor produce outputs that mimic specific real voices. But in Friday’s complaint, the Elvis owners say those claims are “unequivocally false.” They included links to videos capturing the use of Suno’s platform to play songs that sound remarkably similar to Presley.

“Those … are NOT examples of Elvis Presley singing. They are synthetic and unlicensed uses of Elvis’ voice and likeness,” Busch writes. “There are hundreds to thousands more like it.”

The new case will test the power and limits of the ELVIS (Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security) Act, a law enacted in 2024 in Presley’s adopted home state to make it easier for musicians to bring such cases. Existing laws typically only applied to commercial exploitation of someone’s likeness, like an unauthorized advertisement; the new statute removed those restrictions. ELVIS also specifically imposed liability on companies that provide tools allowing for unauthorized use of a person’s likeness.

“Suno is the embodiment of why the ELVIS Act was so essentially required,” the lawsuit reads. “Suno has stolen Elvis’ voice, his image, and likeness, as well as his copyrighted works on, literally, a breathtaking scale, and must now be called to answer for its theft.”

Suno’s lawyers have argued such claims won’t hold up in court. In an earlier likeness case filed by Jason Isbell and other artists, the AI firm’s lawyers argued it merely uses artist names as “shorthand for the genre they perform in” and does not allow for direct theft of their voices. But the new lawsuit says that as recently as last month, Suno generated an Elvis clone based simply on lyrics that included his name.

“Entering a musician’s name into Suno’s ‘Create’ function, such as Elvis’, causes Suno to generate unauthorized output based on his [name, image and likeness], which copies and reproduces the signature and recognizable aspects of his distinguished voice,” Busch writes in the new case.

In addition to the new voice claims, the lawsuit echoes the same accusations made against Anthropic over training on copyrighted Elvis songs, including “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” arguably Presley’s most famous track; “Don’t Be Cruel,” one of his early massive hits; and “A Little Less Conversation,” “All Shook Up,” “Return to Sender” and “(You’re the) Devil in Disguise”. And like the earlier case, the new lawsuit claims Suno stole those songs in order to replace human artists.

“The next Elvis won’t pick up a guitar,” the Presley Enterprises lawyers write. “Suno’s ravenous race to the bottom aims to make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect.”

Separately on Friday, the same attorneys another case against Suno on behalf of Eight Mile Style, a publisher that owns much of Eminem’s catalog. That case includes similar copyright allegations as the Elvis case, accusing the lab of training its models on the rapper’s “Lose Yourself,” “Without Me,” “Till I Collapse,” “The Real Slim Shady, “Stan” and other hits.

The Elvis and Eminem cases add to mounting legal challenges for Suno. The company was first sued in 2024 by all three major music companies over AI training. Though it settled with Warner Music Group last year and has vowed to partner with the music industry, is still litigating with UMG and Sony Music — who have shown no interest in striking a deal. It has also faced new cases in recent months from music publishers Round Hill Music and Reservoir, as well as the Isbell case over likenesses.

#743. Ariana Grande Shares Intimate Glimpse at Ricky Álvarez Romance

Ariana Grande and her boyfriend Ricky Álvarez showed off PDA in a new social media video as they gave each other kisses while doing a viral challenge for her makeup brand R.E.M Beauty.

Ariana Grande is telling Ricky Álvarez to come on and put her lipstick on.

The “petal” singer shared an inside look at her sweet romance with her boyfriend as the couple showed off some major PDA while taking on a social media challenge for Grande’s makeup brand R.E.M. Beauty.

In a Nov. 7 Instagram Reel, the Grammy winner tasked Álvarez with guessing which R.E.M Beauty lip products she was wearing on her lips only through blind kisses as the 35-year-old had his beanie covering his eyes.

“This is a challenge called, ‘What’s on my lips?’” Grande shared, kicking off the clip, to which Álvarez quipped, “Or what’s on my girlfriend’s lips, really.”

The Wicked actress—who was sitting on Álvarez’s lap—first applied a generous layer of lip gloss, before giving her man a smooch.

And Álvarez proved he doesn’t need space, asking Grande for another kiss.

“Oh, I need more,” he admitted, to which Grande kissed him again. “That’s not Blur Butter.”

“It has to be Glossy Balm,” Álvarez went on. “I don’t have a tingle yet. I also just ate spicy ramen, so I feel like the pores would be open. I feel like it might hit me quicker, so I think I’m gonna go with Glossy Balm.”

Grande cheerfully declared to her man that he was correct.

Álvarez was ready to say thank u, next as he guessed the next two rounds correctly, with Grande continuing to give her boyfriend more loving smooches.

And the dancer showed how much he knows his girlfriend’s brand one last time for a “bonus round,” correctly guessing a lip product that seemingly hadn’t been released yet.

“Interesting, not one of the ones I’m used to. Is it Holiday Mélange?” Álvarez asked Grande, who shared with a laugh that he was right. “I don’t think that one’s out yet.”

He also seems to love the way the Focker-In-Law actress runs R.E.M. After all, Álvarez noted during the video how the brand’s products are made in Italy, with Grande even highlighting the moment in the comments section of the video.

And as the pair—who first dated from 2015 until 2016, before confirming their reconciliation in August—continue to show off their big feelings for one another, Grande has expressed she hopes this love will be forever tattooed on her heart.

During the final show of her Eternal Sunshine Tour in September, the 33-year-old once again changed the lyrics to line about Álvarez in “thank u, next.”

Instead of singing, “Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh,” Grande sang, “Wrote some songs about Ricky / I’m tryna make him my last.”

For a closer look at Grande’s romantic history, keep reading…

Though Ariana Grande and actor Graham Phillips have since gone their separate ways, the pair have proved they certainly can be friends.

The Grammy winner and The Good Wife alum met in 2008 while starring in the hit Broadway musical 13.

And while the duo may have called it quits in 2011, it’s obvious they’ve remained on good terms, sharing a selfie from a “Lil 13 reunion” they had in 2016 and enjoying a 2019 dinner together in New York.

While it’s a true story that Jai Brooks dated Grande for nearly two years, their on-again off-again relationship wasn’t always full of sweetener.

Indeed, the Australian YouTuber shot his shot with Grande over X (formerly Twitter) in 2012 as part of a challenge with twin brother Luke Brooks. The siblings—part of YouTube comedy group The Janoskians—competed to see who could get the Nickelodeon star’s attention first.

After putting out a July 2012 video outlining why the child star should date him, the pair began a long-distance relationship that lasted into 2013.

Following the breakup, Brooks took to X to accuse Grande of cheating on him with The Wanted’s Nathan Sykes, a claim she denied.

"I'm going to be the lady my mother raised and carry myself with class and dignity... But I will never be any man's press opportunity…” she wrote on X at the time. “It's always ok to defend yourself. My fans know what kind of person I am. Never let any man discredit u or the values you were raised with...I'm finally happy. Words can't hurt me anymore.”

Despite the back-and-forth, Grande and Brooks poured into their relationship one last time, reconciling in 2014, though they walked away from their connection for good months later.

After Grande and Sykes collaborated on their 2013 duet "Almost Is Never Enough,” Grande knew the boy was hers. Though the pair dated publicly for about five months, Grande told Brian Fink of Florida radio's 93.3 FLZ in December of that year that they’d broken up and remained “really good friends.”

In 2016, they teamed up yet again for their track “Over and Over Again.” And while there were some post-breakup jitters when it came to working together again, Sykes—who married wife Charlotte Burke in October 2025—detailed how he and the Wicked star quickly moved past any uncomfortable vibes.

"I spoke to [Ariana] and I was like, 'It's only as awkward as everyone else makes it,'" Sykes told Entertainment Tonight at the time. "If we don't make it awkward, then at the end of the day, after a couple of weeks, it's not going to be awkward anymore."

Romance rumors began about Grande and Big Sean—who had previously collaborated on tracks like “Best Mistake” and “Right There”—after they were spotted leaving a movie theater together in August 2014.

One month later, the “Blessings” rapper subtly confirmed their relationship.

"That Ariana is very, very special,” he said during his appearance on On Air with Ryan Seacrest in September 2014. “She's very special to me.”

And while the “thank u, next” hitmaker thought she’d end up with Sean, he wasn’t a match.

Grande and Sean—who welcomed son Noah with longtime partner Jhené Aiko in 2022—broke up in April 2015 after nearly nine months of dating due to conflicting tour schedules, a source previously told E! News.

In a joint statement, Grande and Sean’s reps shared they "care deeply for each other and remain close friends."

Mac Miller first teamed up with Grande professionally on a 2012 cover of “Baby It’s Cold Outside”—and later their 2013 single “The Way”—before their connection turned romantic.

Though they sparked dating rumors early on in their working relationship, Miller set the record straight after their steamy music video for the latter track raised eyebrows about the nature of their connection.

“That’s the homie. She’s got a boyfriend and everything,” Miller told MTV News in an April 2013 interview, referencing her romance with Brooks. “Obviously, that [kiss] made everyone talk. I didn’t even know that was going to happen and then we were shooting and the director was like, ‘This should happen,’ and I’m like, ‘Alright.’”

But it seems Miller was more game for the interaction than he let on. After all, the pair went public with their relationship in August 2016 while attending the MTV VMAs together.

Though they were able to collaborate on many more tracks together—including  “My Favorite Part” from Miller’s 2016 album The Divine Feminine—it was how they supported each other in the face of hardship that made their romance so strong.

After the terrorist bombing at Grande’s 2017 concert in Manchester—which claimed the lives of 22 people—Miller stood by her side, later joining her on stage at the benefit show she hosted to support the victims.

But in May 2018, Grande and Miller broke up.

“This is one of my best friends in the whole world and favorite people on the planet,” Grande wrote on Instagram Stories at the time. “I respect and adore him endlessly and am grateful to have him in my life in any form, at all times regardless of how our relationship changes or what the universe holds for each of us!”

Four months later, Miller tragically died following an accidental overdose. It wasn’t until a year later that Grande spoke publicly about her profound grief.

“It’s pretty all-consuming,” she told Vogue in a July 2019 interview. “By no means was what we had perfect, but, like, f--k. He was the best person ever, and he didn’t deserve the demons he had.”

“I was the glue for such a long time, and I found myself becoming less and less sticky,” she added. “The pieces just started to float away.”

Did Grande and Pete Davidson have the ultimate whirlwind romance? Yes, and?

The comedian made his relationship with the “Dangerous Woman” singer Instagram official in May 2018 after they met on Saturday Night Live.

Weeks later, Davidson debuted multiple tattoos in Grande’s honor before confirming his engagement to the “Into You” singer one month later.

“I feel like I won a contest, so sick,” Davidson said of the engagement during his June 2018 appearance on the Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. “It’s f--king lit, Jimmy. It’s so lit.”

In August, the pair made their romance red carpet-official as they attended the 2018 MTV Video Music Awards together, just days after Grande dropped her fourth studio album Sweetener, which features the song “pete davidson.”

While they covered quite a bit of ground in their relationship together, Grande and Davidson—who has since welcomed a daughter Scottie Rose with ex Elsie Hewitt—broke up in October 2018, but not without Grande giving her former fiancé one last shoutout.

As Grande sings in “thank u, next,” “Even almost got married / And for Pete, I’m so thankful.”

And it wasn’t all that long after Grande’s split from Davidson that she found herself walking down the aisle holding hands with her mama.

She and Dalton Gomez began dating in the beginning of 2020, right before the COVID-19 pandemic put the pair on lockdown. The “yes, and?” singer and real estate agent quarantined together, making their love Instagram official that June.

And by December of that year, they imagined a world together as they got engaged.

Five months later, the pair tied the knot at their home in Montecito, California.

“They got married. It was tiny and intimate—less than 20 people,” Grande’s rep told People of the May 2021 nuptials. “The room was so happy and full of love. The couple and both families couldn’t be happier.”

But Grande and Gomez broke free from their marriage just two years later before settling the terms of their divorce in October 2023, according to documents obtained by E! News.

Per the agreement, according to TMZ, Gomez received a one-time tax-free payment of $1,250,000 and half the net proceeds of their L.A. home sale but did not collect spousal support.

Grande and Dalton finalized their divorce in March 2024.

Grande first discoverated her feelings for Ethan Slater on the set of Wicked before their romance began in July 2023. Two months later, they were seen on a Disney World date in photos obtained by TMZ.

A source close to Grande and Slater told E! News after the excursion, “they went with a big group of friends including her mom and brother and are really happy and really good for each other.”

And while the pair’s thrillifying romance got a stamp of approval from Grande’s brother Frankie Grande, who called him a “very sweet guy” in a June 2024 interview with TooFab, the couple’s relationship became the center of controversy following speculation there was overlap with their previous marriages.

“It definitely doesn’t get any easier, seeing some of the negativity that was birthed by disreputable tabloids,” Grande told Vanity Fair in 2024 of the chatter. “Of course, I went through a lot of life changes during the filming of this movie. A lot of people that were working on it did.”

Grande went on to defend Slater—who welcomed a son with ex-wife Lilly Jay in August 2022—against any negativity thrown at him.

“There couldn’t be a less accurate depiction of a human being than the one that the tabloids spread about him,” Grande added. “No one on this earth tries harder or spreads themselves thinner to be there for the people that he loves and cares about. There is no one on this earth with a better heart, and that is something that no bullshit tabloid can rewrite in real life.”

That same month, Slater finalized his divorce with Jay.

Following the changes in his personal life, the Broadway star opened up about the challenges of being catapulted into the spotlight.

“I think there was something that was really difficult about things in your private life being commented on and looked at by the public,” Slater told GQ in 2024. “There were a lot of big changes in private lives that were really happening, so it’s really hard to see people who don’t know anything about what’s happening commenting on it.”

While breakup rumors between the two began in late 2025, they called their three-year romance off for good in June 2026.

Grande and Ricky Álvarez’s love story began in 2015 after he joined the popstar on her Honeymoon Tour as a background dancer.

“We’re happy,” Grande told Billboard of her romance with Álvarez in a May 2016 interview. “I’m a very happy girl. I have a healthy life right now, and I think that’s all anyone cares to know. The end.”

Their romance proved to be short and sweet, with the musician and the professional dancer calling it quits just months later in July 2016.

But there were brighter days ahead for the couple, who were seen together during a June 2026 group lunch at De Nada Cantina in Austin.

One day later, Grande switched up the lyrics to her 2018 hit “thank u, next.” Though she usually followed the lyric, “Wrote some song about Ricky,” with, “now I listen and laugh,” at her Austin show she said, “They still really slap.”

Weeks later, she was back at it again, this time singing at her July 13 concert, “We always find our way back.”

Soon after, he found his way onto her grid, with Grande appearing to soft launch their romance on Instagram July 27 ahead of the release of her eighth album Petal.

As she captioned the post which included a clip of herself clinking olives with Álvarez, “petal season continued …….. !”

On Aug. 2, 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across Tunisia, giving Star Wars fans a rare chance to experience a total solar eclipse at the real-life filming locations of Tatooine.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Aug. 2, 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across some of the most iconic filming locations from Star Wars, plunging them into darkness during what's being called the "eclipse of the century".

The path of the 2027 total solar eclipse will cross southern Tunisia, where several locations were used to bring the fictional desert planet Tatooine to life. From the dunes of Mos Espa to the rocky Jundland Wastes, Star Wars fans will have the rare opportunity to experience totality at the very places where their favorite scenes were filmed

But not every famous filming location will experience totality, so choosing where to watch will be crucial. Here are four locations that fall directly in the moon's shadow. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date.

Location: south of Chott el-Gharsa, Tozeur Governorate, southwest Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 2 minutes, 9 seconds

With a massive budget and three prequels to make, Lucasfilm built a new film set that would double as the Mos Espa spaceport on Tatooine for The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones. This is where Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jar Jar Binks and Padme get stranded, where they meet Anakin Skywalker and where the podrace takes place. Now abandoned, it's in the middle of nowhere, between two huge salt lakes and subject to the intense heat and moving Eriguet dunes — but it is firmly within the path of totality. Nearby are two other shooting locations — the Ong Jemel outcrop, where Darth Maul arrives on the scene, and Yardang, where Qui-Gon and Darth Maul battle — the first-ever lightsaber duel filmed on location.

Location: Jebel Sidi Bouhlel canyon, Dghoumès National Park, Tozeur, southwest Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 37 seconds

Often called "Star Wars Canyon" by fans and crew, Maguer Gorge in Jebel Sidi Bouhlel doubled as the Jundland Wastes of Tatooine in Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope. It's where Luke Skywalker is attacked by Tusken Raiders, where Obi-Wan Kenobi first appears and where Luke and Obi-Wan discover the slaughtered Jawas. The canyon also provided the distant view of Mos Eisley — the famous "wretched hive of scum and villainy." On Aug. 2, 2027, you'll likely be pointing your macrobinoculars at the eclipsed sun rather than Tusken Raiders.

Steven Spielberg later filmed here for Raiders of the Lost Ark, including the scene in which Indiana Jones threatens to destroy the Ark with a bazooka. Just south of Dghoumès National Park is a desert oasis called Bouhlel Sdada, used for the archaeological dig scenes in Raiders.

Location: Ajim city center, Médenine Governorate, Djerba island, Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:10 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 55 seconds

Djerba Island's palm trees, beaches and Mediterranean horizons will make it a popular destination for eclipse chasers after a long totality away from the heat and crowds of Luxor in Egypt. It's also home to three notable Star Wars filming locations. The original movie's Mos Eisley footage was shot here, with Ajim doubling as a Stormtrooper checkpoint ("These are not the droids you're looking for"), the Cantina exterior, and an alley near Docking Bay 94 where stormtroopers watch the Millennium Falcon blast off. In reality, it's an abandoned bakery.

Location: Ajim outskirts, Médenine Governorate, Djerba island, Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:09 a.m. CET; 4 minutes

Just north of Ajim, this mosque — originally a fisherman's house — was used as a stand-in for "Old Ben's" house, where Obi-Wan Kenobi gives Luke Skywalker a lightsaber. It was used purely for photography, and no actors set foot here. It was also cut from the movie's Special Edition in 1997, so you'll only find it in the original version. Completists might also want to check out Sidi Jemour Mosque to the north, which was used for scenes with Biggs Darklighter that didn't even make the final cut. IYKYK …

Tunisia's Star Wars locations are spread across the south, so the easiest way to see several is on an organized tour or with a private driver and guide. Tozeur is the main base for visiting Mos Espa, Ong Jemel and Jebel Sidi Bouhlel, with local operators offering half-day and full-day 4x4 excursions into the desert. Djerba Island is the other major hub for three sights. Longer multi-day tours typically connect Tozeur with Matmata, home to Hotel Sidi Idriss — the Lars Homestead — as well as Djerba.

One tour company, Star Wars Tours, is running a (sold-out) special departure called "Eclipse tour from the Outer Rim" that witnesses totality at the Mos Espa set. Other Star Wars-focused tour operators include Galaxy Tours, though one-day trips to the Mos Espa set from Tozeur are also available.

Tunisia is surely one of the most attractive destinations for the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse. Historical cloud cover is exceptionally low, while totality reaches around five and a half minutes near the centerline. It also offers established tourism infrastructure and generally lower August temperatures than Egypt, making it an obvious alternative for eclipse chasers hoping to avoid the biggest crowds around Luxor.

You can, of course, visit the Star Wars sets in the days before or after the eclipse. For Tunisia's maximum duration of totality, consider Sfax, where darkness lasts 5 minutes, 41 seconds, or nearby Chaffar Beach, with its long, open Mediterranean coastline. Offshore, the low-lying Kerkennah Islands get around 5 minutes, 39 seconds. Inland, Sidi Bouzid offers about 5 minutes, 33 seconds beneath typically dry skies, while the spectacular Roman amphitheater at El Jem gets 4 minutes, 23 seconds. On Djerba Island, meanwhile, beaches and extensive resort infrastructure make combining an eclipse chase with a conventional Mediterranean vacation particularly easy — with a view of Mos Eisley thrown in for good measure.

Jamie is an experienced science and travel journalist, stargazer and eclipse chaser who writes about exploring the night sky, solar and lunar eclipses, the Northern Lights, moon-gazing, astro-travel, astronomy and space exploration. He is the editor of WhenIsTheNextEclipse.com, author of A Stargazing Program For Beginners, co-author of The Eclipse Effect, and a senior contributor at Forbes.

#741. Richard Lloyd, Television Guitarist, Dies at 75

The musician was diagnosed with bile duct cancer in March 2026.

Richard Lloyd, a founding member and guitarist of influential New York rock band Television, has died. He was 75.

Lloyd died Saturday morning (Nov. 7) at his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee, according to to Rolling Stone.

“His loving wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays were with him at the end,” his family told the publication.

His cause of death was cholangiocarcinoma, a cancer of the bile ducts. Lloyd was diagnosed with the disease in March 2026, and a GoFundMe campaign was later launched to help cover his medical expenses and other bills.

Born in Pittsburgh in 1951, Lloyd moved with his family to New York City at age 6 and grew up in Greenwich Village. He initially studied drums before turning to guitar. After spending time in Boston and Los Angeles, he returned to New York in 1973.

That year, he joined forces with Tom Verlaine, Richard Hell and drummer Billy Ficca to form Television. The band became a regular at CBGB, the Lower Manhattan club that helped launch the careers of fellow New York acts including the Ramones, the New York Dolls, Talking Heads, and Blondie.

Television released its debut album, Marquee Moon, in 1977. The album earned widespread critical acclaim for its intricate arrangements and the distinctive interplay between Lloyd’s and Verlaine’s guitars. Although it achieved limited commercial success, the album went on to become one of the most influential releases of its era. The group followed it with Adventure in 1978 before breaking up later that year.

Lloyd launched his solo career with the 1979 release of Alchemy, but struggles with substance abuse derailed his career in the years that followed. After getting sober, he returned with his second solo album, Field of Fire, in 1985. He continued releasing music over the following decades, with his final solo studio album, The Countdown, arriving in 2018.

He also worked as a session guitarist, contributing to recordings by artists including Matthew Sweet and John Doe of X, while continuing to tour and teach guitar. In 2017, he published his memoir, Everything Is Combustible: Television, CBGB’s and Five Decades of Rock and Roll.

Television reunited to record its self-titled third album, released in 1992, and continued performing periodically in the years that followed. Lloyd announced his departure from the band in 2007 to focus on his solo career.
